key_insight: Multiple flexible leaflets in a confined low-Re flow can collectively rectify symmetric oscillations into a net transport, with strongest pumping at high leaflet density and an optimal elastoviscous balance.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest a design rule for microfluidic pumps and biomimetic transport devices: tune leaflet spacing and stiffness to maximize flow rectification under oscillatory actuation.
method: Numerical study of interacting asymmetric leaflets in a channel at low Reynolds number
Use of symmetrically oscillating plates to remove background flow asymmetries
Analytical steady-limit framework extended to time-dependent channel oscillations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a combined numerical and analytical evaluation showing that net transport increases with leaflet density and peaks at an optimal elastoviscous number.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on an idealized low-Re, confined geometry, so real devices may be sensitive to fabrication tolerances, leaflet wear, and unmodeled 3D effects.
paper_title: On the rectification of oscillatory flows by flexible leaflets in a confined geometry
